title: bounded opportunistic credit allocator and utilization fingerprinting
author: Avery Chen
description:
Motivation: Dedicated fleets occasionally show short-duration microbursts that the existing reservation/burst systems either over-provision for (wasting headroom) or under-account for (causing SLA slippage). This PR introduces two coordinated pieces: (1) a bounded opportunistic credit allocator that hands out limited short-lived credits for transient bursts without inflating long-term reservations, and (2) a compact utilization fingerprint that captures fine-grained temporal usage patterns to inform credit pacing and more accurate autoscaler smoothing.

Summary of changes: implement credit allocator logic, persist per-pool credit ledgers, add a small state machine to revoke credits when sustained usage is detected, add a util-fingerprint sampler and serializer, expose fingerprint histograms to telemetry, wire decisions into the autoscaler admission path, and provide a feature flag and rollout toggles.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (ENG-2137) - [x] Unit and integration tests for allocator state machine - [x] Telemetry + Grafana panels added - [x] Feature flag + canary rollout plan included - [x] Backwards-compatible gating so older nodes ignore fingerprints

Design notes and links: The opportunistic credit allocator issues time-bounded credits up to a per-tenant and per-pool cap. Credits are leaky (decay) and are removed deterministically when utilization fingerprints indicate the burst is sustained above threshold T_sustain. The utilization fingerprint is a 64-byte Bloom-style sketch of octave-bucketed short-window QPS/latency patterns (10ms buckets over 5s windows sampled every 1s) which is cheap to compute on serving nodes and mergeable for cluster-level views. See design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-2137/opportunistic-crediting-and-util-fingerprint for motivation and math.

Rollout: feature flag new.credit_allocator.enabled (default off). Canary on 3 pools for 48h, monitor credit churn, SLA p95 latency, and credit-induced fallbacks. If credit churn > 30% or p95 regression > 5% roll back.

Backwards compatibility: nodes that do not understand fingerprints will ignore the header and the allocator falls back to existing burst paths. No schema changes to persisted reservations were made.

Author notes: This approach aims to reduce long-term reservation inflation while improving short-burst acceptance. The fingerprint is intentionally lossy and tuned for signal-to-noise; it is not intended for billing or audit.
